summary: Ephemeral session-affinity mismatch triggers fallback routing during staged canary promote
description:
Issue summary: During a staged promote of redwood-rw-13b-v1 to 40% canary weight for ArcLens dedicated cluster, a subset of long-lived sessions lost expected version affinity and were routed to fallback model variants, causing degraded responses and increased latency. Impact: ~6% of user sessions for ArcLens produced responses from a fallback quantized variant or returned transient 502s for 3 minutes. Customers reported content mismatches and slower response times.

Timeline: 2026-02-25 14:12 UTC - Canary weight change pushed from 10% to 40%. 14:15 UTC - First customer report to #support. 14:20 UTC - Automated alert: spike in 5xxs and tail latency on us-east serving fleet. 14:22 UTC - Support created ticket and engaged SRE.

Environment: ArcLens dedicated pool (customer-owned VPC peering), serving-runtime v3.8.1, routing-reconciler v2.14.

Observed behavior: A portion of sessions that had previously been pinned to the stable model lost their session affinity when requests hit edge proxies that had stale session-token maps. The routing layer then applied fallback policies (model-family fallback and cost-tier fallback) and routed requests to the quantized variant; some requests hit a transient 502 from a GPU node being drained. Expected behavior: Session affinity should persist for pinned sessions during staged promotes; fallbacks should not be invoked for pinned sessions unless explicit health checks fail.

Customer impact: ArcLens reported incorrect predictive scores for some cohorts and elevated error rates affecting visible dashboards.

Temporary workaround: Rolled back canary weight to 10% and forced session-affinity reconciliation for ArcLens tenant via admin API to rebind sessions to pinned version.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Have a dedicated customer pool with session pinning enabled and long-lived conversations (session TTL > 10m).
2) Start traffic that establishes session-affinity tokens and pins to redwood-rw-13b-v1 stable variant.
3) Promote a canary by increasing canary weight from 10% to 40% during normal traffic.
4) Observe routing logs and traces for session-token lookup misses at the edge and subsequent fallback routing decisions.

comments: Support (Maya Chen) 2026-02-25T14:20: We received a customer case reporting mismatch between expected stable model outputs and what their app returned after the canary increase. Escalating to SRE and routing owners.

SRE (Diego Ramos) 2026-02-25T14:28: Observed session_lookup misses on a subset of edge proxies. Hypothesis: session-token map TTL and concurrent routing snapshot update caused transient map divergence during rollout. Rolling canary back to 10% and triggering manual session rebind now.
Customer (ArcLens, Emily Park) 2026-02-25T14:35: Thanks — we saw errors clear up after rollback. Please advise on root cause and prevention.

Routing eng (Liam O'Connor) 2026-02-25T15:04: Reproducer identified: concurrent reconcile job bumping routing snapshot while edge cache invalidation still in-flight. Added short-term fix to serialize reconcile commits per-tenant and pushed hotfix to reconciler (PR #1284).
SRE (Diego Ramos) 2026-02-27T09:12: Post-fix monitoring shows no recurrence on us-east. Will run a focused chaos test for edge cache eviction patterns overnight.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: model pin eviction due to canary promotion race with snapshot commit. Evidence: router-edge logs show session_lookup misses correlated with reconcile commit timestamps.

Detailed trace: requests with session_token present at client arrived at edge-02 which had not yet applied the new routing snapshot but had a cleared session map; reconciler commit created a short window where tokens were considered stale by the edge cache eviction logic.

Reconciler change: prior behavior allowed concurrent snapshot writes for the same tenant leading to brief inconsistent state; hotfix ensures reconcile commits are serialized and includes an atomic session-map swap to avoid token TTL races.

Additional contributing factor: a GPU drain initiated nearby caused a handful of 502s which triggered fallback policy; if not for the affinity miss, those requests would have retried to pinned nodes instead of fallback variant.
resolution:
Applied immediate mitigations: 1) Rolled canary back to 10% for ArcLens at 14:26 UTC; 2) Triggered manual session-affinity reconciliation for the tenant; 3) Deployed reconciler hotfix (PR #1284) which serializes per-tenant snapshot commits and performs atomic session-map swaps; 4) Added short-term safeguard to defer fallback routing for requests that include a valid session-token within a 30s reconciliation window. Post-deploy monitoring for 48h showed no reappearance of the issue.

Follow-ups and action items: Create an automated regression test that simulates concurrent reconcile + edge eviction; add telemetry to alert when session_lookup miss rate spikes above 0.5% during rollouts; update canary runbook to include manual session rebind step for dedicated customers with long-lived sessions. Postmortem and long-term design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/98765/2026-02-25+Session+Affinity+Fallback+Postmortem
next_steps: 1) Implement regression test in staging to reproduce concurrent snapshot + edge eviction scenario (owner: routing team, due: 2026-03-05).
